problem: Feedback and feature requests are scattered across channels.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Research complaints and willingness to pay before treating this as demand.
solution_hypothesis: a lightweight inbox that groups repeated requests into a prioritized backlog
publish_text: A creator can get the same feature request in a DM, a comment, an email and a community thread. The hard part isn't collecting feedback. It's noticing what's being asked for repeatedly. How do you track that today?

problem: Scope changes and assumptions can quietly erode project margins.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Validate with public discussions and paid competitor products.
solution_hypothesis: a project scoping workbook with explicit assumptions and change approvals
publish_text: Scope creep rarely arrives as one dramatic request. It's a handful of tiny “while you're in there…” changes. Freelancers, how do you document assumptions and approve extra work without making every project feel bureaucratic?

problem: Stock, fees, reorder levels and margins often live in disconnected sheets.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Check competing templates and seller complaints.
solution_hypothesis: an inventory workbook that combines reorder signals with per-item margins
publish_text: A product can look profitable until marketplace fees, packaging, shipping and restocking time are counted. For small sellers, which number is easiest to lose track of: true margin, stock on hand, or reorder timing?

problem: Follow-ups, interview notes and application stages get lost across tabs.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Compare job trackers and user complaints before building.
solution_hypothesis: a focused job-search tracker with role-specific notes and follow-up reminders
publish_text: Job searching can turn into a spreadsheet graveyard: application status in one tab, follow-ups in another, interview notes in your inbox. What part of staying organised is still painful, even with existing trackers?

problem: Good reader questions and story ideas disappear between issues.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Look for repeated creator workflows and existing paid alternatives.
solution_hypothesis: an editorial backlog that turns reader feedback into tagged story candidates
publish_text: Reader replies can contain better story ideas than a blank editorial calendar. The problem is remembering them when it's time to write the next issue. Newsletter writers, how do you save reader questions and decide which ones deserve a piece?

problem: Leads, quotes and follow-ups are easy to forget when the owner does everything.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Interview operators and inspect existing low-cost tools.
solution_hypothesis: a simple quote and follow-up tracker designed for one-person businesses
publish_text: For a one-person service business, the job isn't over when the quote is sent. Remembering to follow up is its own admin task. What do you use to track quotes that haven't turned into bookings yet?

problem: Group-project decisions and task ownership can vanish in chat histories.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Validate with students and compare existing group-work apps.
solution_hypothesis: a lightweight decision log and responsibility tracker for small teams
publish_text: Group projects don't usually need another giant task board. They need decisions that don't vanish in chat and a clear owner for the next step. What tools have actually worked for student teams beyond week one?

problem: Vendor quotes, deadlines and last-minute changes are spread across documents.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Research organizer forums and paid planning templates.
solution_hypothesis: an event operations workbook that connects budgets, vendors and deadlines
publish_text: A small event means vendor quotes, payment dates, guest counts and last-minute changes competing for attention. Event organisers, what's the one spreadsheet or checklist you wish you'd set up sooner?

problem: Launch feedback arrives before makers have a repeatable way to categorize it.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Review launch discussions and creator tools before claiming demand.
solution_hypothesis: a launch feedback triage board with tags for bugs, requests and objections
publish_text: A launch can produce dozens of comments and still leave a maker unsure what to fix first. Bugs, feature requests and “I don't get it” feedback need different treatment. How do indie builders sort launch feedback today?

problem: Discovery calls produce notes that rarely become a clear action plan.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Validate against consulting workflows and paid templates.
solution_hypothesis: a discovery-call worksheet that turns client goals into measurable deliverables
publish_text: A discovery call can feel productive, then a week later the notes are still just notes. Consultants, what process actually turns client goals into deliverables and next actions you follow through on?

problem: Useful long-form ideas are difficult to adapt consistently across formats.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Research creator feedback and the crowded repurposing-tool market.
solution_hypothesis: a structured repurposing planner that maps one core idea to several distinct formats
publish_text: Repurposing content shouldn't mean copy-pasting one idea into five formats. The useful part is finding a different angle for each audience. What helps you reuse an idea without making every post feel recycled?

problem: Repeated support questions can expose product friction but are hard to summarize.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Explore founder forums and lightweight support products.
solution_hypothesis: a support-theme tracker that groups recurring questions into documentation tasks
publish_text: Repeated support questions can be a product signal, not just a support problem. If customers keep asking the same thing, the UI or docs may be failing them. How do small SaaS teams spot those patterns?

problem: Product updates, file versions and customer-facing change notes can drift apart.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Check how existing marketplaces and sellers handle updates.
solution_hypothesis: a version and release-note checklist for downloadable products
publish_text: A downloadable product changes, but the updated file, version notes and customer instructions don't always change together. Digital-product sellers, how do you manage updates without leaving buyers confused?

problem: Boxes and household items become difficult to locate after moving.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Research moving checklists, inventory apps and user complaints.
solution_hypothesis: a printable and searchable moving inventory with box labels and room mapping
publish_text: Moving-day mystery: you know the charger is in one of the boxes, but which one? I'm exploring simple home-inventory ideas. Do you label boxes in a way that makes unpacking genuinely easier?

problem: Learning plans often track hours spent rather than evidence of practical skill.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Compare career trackers and portfolio-based learning methods.
solution_hypothesis: a project-evidence tracker linking skills to demos, code and interview stories
publish_text: Hours studied are easy to track. Proof that you can do the job is harder. For a career switch, shipped projects, demos and clear explanations seem more useful than a streak counter. How do you track evidence of skill?

problem: Client approvals and pending assets block delivery without a visible reason.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Validate through agency workflows and competitor reviews.
solution_hypothesis: a client handoff checklist that highlights missing approvals and assets
publish_text: A project can be “almost done” for days because one client approval or missing asset is blocking everything. Small agencies, how do you make the next blocker obvious without adding another status meeting?

problem: Market notes, competitor examples and assumptions become mixed together.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Inspect founder research workflows before building.
solution_hypothesis: a research ledger that separates sourced observations from assumptions and decisions
publish_text: Founder research gets messy when a sourced observation, a hunch and a product decision all end up in the same document. What do you use to keep evidence separate from assumptions?

problem: Learner questions can reveal confusing lessons but rarely make it into the next revision.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Research educator communities and course feedback tools.
solution_hypothesis: a lesson feedback tracker that connects learner confusion to specific course sections
publish_text: If learners keep asking the same question, it may be a lesson problem, not a learner problem. Course creators, how do you connect repeated confusion to the exact lesson that needs fixing?

problem: Pricing can omit packaging, marketplace fees and time spent making each item.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Compare existing costing calculators and seller discussions.
solution_hypothesis: a costing sheet that shows contribution margin after fees, materials and labour
publish_text: Handmade pricing gets tricky when materials are counted but labour, packaging, marketplace fees and failed attempts aren't. Sellers, what costs do you include before deciding a price?

problem: Small commitments and next actions get buried across notes and task apps.
evidence: Unverified hypothesis. Validate against established task tools and public complaints.
solution_hypothesis: a weekly side-project review sheet that limits active work and captures next actions
publish_text: A side-project list can become a graveyard of good intentions. The hard part is deciding what stays active and what gets parked. Do you use a weekly review, a limit on active projects, or something else?
